system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “standard,” “cleared” and “accepted” labels are assertions, not buyer approval. I have assessed the draft against Wattlebridge’s playbook and the facts actually stated in the Disclosure Letter; it does not establish matters the letter expressly leaves unverified.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none is given. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The fallback is not authorised merely because the Seller proposes it. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** basket, with recovery only above the basket. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** aggregate basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; propose the playbook thresholds and tipping basket.** The Seller’s thresholds are materially less protective. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | **18 months** after Completion; limits apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | **24 months** for general claims; separate regimes for Fundamental/Title claims and protected carve-outs. | **Reject 18 months; seek 24 months.** The 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties under the same caps and time limits as general warranties. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; draft a separate Fundamental/Title regime.** Administrative simplicity does not override the specific buyer position. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; this cannot be waived. | **Reject; require an express comprehensive carve-out.** The Seller’s blanket wording would otherwise swallow the required protection. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, alongside specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject general disclosure; retain only specific, fair disclosures.** The letter’s broad references do not identify fairly the matters relied on to qualify warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions. If any qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Reject; delete the blanket exclusion.** Discovery or access to data-room material is not buyer approval or a substitute for Seller responsibility. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure Letter says final consent and evidence conditions are **not included**. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Reject consent-on-delivery; make both items a pre-Completion condition.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the letter does not establish consent or condition satisfaction. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release to follow Completion. Letter says facility is unpaid and no final discharge is included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release as drafted.** The facility remains unpaid and no discharge is evidenced. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** bonuses left out of funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. On-costs unspecified. | Treat DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded obligation; ensure no silent exclusion. | **Require express allocation and funding treatment before signing/completion.** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and the funds flow omits them. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. Letter says **AUD 180,000** is not independent bank verification and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; do not assume either payment or non-payment is verified. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it subject to the cure.** The transfer condition depends on cleared payment, but the disclosed amount is unverified and assignment is unconfirmed. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material. Letter says access, scope and notification duty are unresolved; no loss amount stated. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Require preservation, investigation and ongoing updates; do not assert a confirmed breach or amount.** The disclosed facts are preliminary and do not establish access, harm or a notification duty. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are ordinary-course operating costs. Letter leaves avoidability, termination, accrual and ordinary-course status unresolved. | Assess the renewals; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess; make no automatic Debt or price adjustment.** The Seller’s characterisation is not established by the disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; tax and IP described as settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden override by general limitations. | **Reject the blanket override and preserve distinct category treatment.** The Seller’s wording risks collapsing separately negotiated regimes into general liability limits. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register said to evidence title to 100% of shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification; do not treat DD-012 alone as conclusive.** The letter identifies the source relied on but does not say the Buyer has verified title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Tax/IP terms remain **open**; do not assume unlimited liability or resolution. | **Keep both topics open for negotiation and review.** The Seller’s assertion does not establish buyer agreement, and the playbook provides no unlimited-liability position. |


=== END ADVICE ===
